subject.title: The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters

sentences.text: Why is the creature closest to this sleeping man holding out a pen?
This is The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters, engraved by Francisco Goya in 1799.
Are these creatures attacking the artist, or working for him?
The first clue is the desk.
The title of the print is written on its front.
The second clue is the sleeper himself.
Many observers believe Goya drew himself asleep among his own drawing tools.
The third clue is Goya's own caption.
According to Goya's caption, fantasy abandoned by reason produces impossible monsters.
United with reason, fantasy is the mother of the arts.
The answer is that these creatures are his own imagination.
Without reason they frighten him, but with it they give him his art.
In Spanish, the word sueño means both sleep and dream.
So the title can also say that the dream of reason produces monsters.
So is Goya sleeping here, or dreaming up his next print?

sources.claim: Los Caprichos, Goya's set of 80 aquatints that were published in the year 1799, emphasize the flaws inherent in humans.
The title of the print, as marked on the front of the desk, is typically read as proclaiming Goya's adherence to the values of the Enlightenment: without reason, evil and corruption prevail.
Many observers believe that Goya intended to depict himself asleep amidst his drawing tools, his reason dulled by slumber, bedeviled by creatures that prowl in the dark.

The full epigraph for Capricho No. 43 reads; "Fantasy abandoned by reason produces impossible monsters: united with her [reason], she [fantasy] is the mother of the arts and the origin of their marvel

Goya also included a caption for this print that may suggest a different interpretation: "Imagination abandoned by reason produces impossible monsters; united with her, she is the mother of the arts a

On this interpretation, Goya believed that imagination should never be completely renounced in favor of the strictly rational, as imagination (in combination with reason) is what produces works of art
